assertions: gDisableStructs[0].isFirstTurn is 1 (not 2) at turn 1's action prompt: TryDoEventsBeforeFirstTurn's own TurnValuesCleanUp(FALSE) already pre-decremented the lead's switch-in value of 2.
It decays 1 -> 0 for BOTH battlers at frame 324, inside turn 1's end-of-turn phase; turn 2's prompt reads [0, 0].
Turn 1 FAKE OUT (isFirstTurn == 1) flinches: 'Foe CHANSEY flinched!'. Turn 2 FAKE OUT (isFirstTurn == 0) prints 'But it failed!' and CHANSEY then acts normally ('Foe CHANSEY used HARDEN!').

Shifting NINJASK in on turn 3 sets isFirstTurn[0] := 2 at frame 1289, and NO 'SPEED BOOST' message appears anywhere in turn 3's end-of-turn window (frames 1291-1664) -- the isFirstTurn != 2 gate is closed on the switch-in turn.
That 2 decays to 1 at frame 1660 (turn 3's TurnValuesCleanUp(FALSE)), and turn 4's end-of-turn fires 'NINJASK's SPEED BOOST raised its SPEED!' with statStages[STAT_SPEED] 6 -> 7 at frame 2250.
isFirstTurn decays 1 -> 0 at frame 2433 and SPEED BOOST fires AGAIN at the end of turn 5 (stage 7 -> 8, frame 3023/3101): the gate is `!= 2`, not `== 0`.
Both battlers' rechargeTimer stays 0 for the whole trace (no recharge move staged); the receipt records the field so the decrement port has a control.
This is semantic RAM evidence sampled on every controller frame; no framebuffer fitting and no runtime oracle dependency.
